clue.text: Obscure hero who espouses lost causes?"

definitions.meaning: ... Fawley is the hero of Thomas Hardy's novel ... the Obscure
The patron saint of lost causes

explanation.surface: A forgotten champion who backs hopeless campaigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective, but it is half of the title of Hardy's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: One reading names Hardy's tragic protagonist; the other names the apostle invoked for desperate cases.

clue.text: Judge concerned with looking cheerful

parts.note: ocular means relating to the eyes and sight

explanation.surface: A judge who looks happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jokey and good-humoured means much the same as cheerful.

clue.text: Protest over first of buses put out of service

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A protest over taking the first bus off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts DEMO above B in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge from the armed forces, releasing someone from military duty.

clue.text: Pound a chewy bit

definitions.meaning: a pound sterling is slang a ...
a plug of tobacco for chewing is also called by this word

explanation.surface: Paying a pound for a piece of something to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a pound coin, and a tobacco plug held in the cheek.

clue.text: Ruined, like John and Anne Donne

definitions.meaning: the poet John Donne, wed to Anne, quipped that the couple were thereby ruined

explanation.surface: A poet and his wife brought to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne's famous pun on his secret marriage: 'John Donne, Anne Donne, Un-done'.
explanation.definitionFit: Destroyed or ruined, and a pun read as a pair of Donnes.

clue.text: Decline to go thus and race on mountain

definitions.meaning: to decline is to go down a slope
a ski race straight down the slope

explanation.surface: Refusing to travel this way in a mountain race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse, but it means deteriorate: to go this way is to decline; 'and' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping downwards, as a worsening trend does, and the fastest alpine skiing event.

clue.text: Best overall range of characters? It's a gem'

parts.note: to top is to beat, and top means best
A to Z covers the whole alphabet, every letter

explanation.surface: The finest complete alphabet of letters is a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow precious stone, so an example of a jewel.

clue.text: A certain sort of sail in fashion that's novel

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces inside the fashion word

parts.note: a trend is a fashion
sure means certain

indicators.note: sort of tells us to arrange the letters of the next word into another order

explanation.surface: A particular kind of sail that is currently stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a type of sail; the wordplay splits the fashion word around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's pirate adventure story is a famous example of a book of fiction.

clue.text: Crossword compiler may assume this to be cryptic

definitions.text: Crossword compiler may assume this to be cryptic

parts.words: Crossword compiler may assume this to be cryptic
parts.note: assume means adopt; setters sign puzzles under a disguising alias to stay unknown

explanation.surface: A setter supposes something is a cryptic puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A false name adopted by a writer, as setters often use.

clue.text: Extra interest surrounding new single, ultimately clownish

annotationWithheld.why: Extra interest surrounding new single, ultimately clownish (7): ZEST round N and I gives ZNIEST; no clue word supplies the A of ZANIEST
annotationWithheld.clue: Extra interest surrounding new single, ultimately clownish

clue.text: Comedians of distinction accompanied by writer

parts.note: laurels are an honour, a mark of distinction
and means together with
Thomas Hardy was a novelist and poet

explanation.surface: Distinguished comic performers in the company of an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan and Ollie were a celebrated double act of film comics.

clue.text: Soldier's forgotten last order

indicators.note: the soldier word has had its final letter dropped, so its end is forgotten

parts.note: a commando is a soldier in a special raiding unit

explanation.surface: A soldier no longer remembers the final instruction given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten last' removes the closing O from COMMANDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct instruction from a superior is synonymous with an order.

clue.text: Now he gets upset about the queen — with what kind of support?

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram surrounds the royal letters
upset means overturned, so these two words are scrambled

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A man is disturbed by something to do with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' scrambles NOW HE into WHEON, which goes 'about' ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word meaning upon which, asking what something rests on.

clue.text: Left by train, for resort with hard maze

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone leaves by rail heading for a holiday town with a tough puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort, scrambling BY TRAIN; 'for' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bewildering network of paths, like the one built for the Minotaur, is a maze.

clue.text: Plant! second border

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A command to plant a second border in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass-like marsh plant with triangular stems.

clue.text: Is that so as to join new league, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise or doubt
read as ..., meaning to ally oneself again, as when signing with a different league

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a club is truly moving to another league.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-ALLY, to form a fresh alliance; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection voicing surprise, and a split reading meaning form an alliance once more.

clue.text: Solemn declaration made in a TV ad, if twice broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the gathered letters are thrown into a new order
twice means the little word is used two times over

explanation.surface: A sworn statement appears in a commercial shown twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles IF; 'broadcast' scrambles A, TV, AD, IF, IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A written statement sworn on oath, used as legal evidence.

clue.text: Popular wine's passed round — one makes notes

indicators.note: the wine is placed around the other piece, so it is passed round it

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A favourite wine circulates at a gathering where someone writes things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests jotting things down, but they are musical notes; 'makes' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument produces musical notes.

clue.text: Restrained humour staged after hours

indicators.note: after places the staged word straight following the abbreviation

parts.note: wit is humour
an event that is held is staged

explanation.surface: A comedy show put on late at night was toned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restrained' looks like a past-tense verb about humour, but it is the definition: kept back.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept back or refused, as with information not released.

clue.text: If one crashes into vehicle, it may be sobering!

indicators.note: into says the scrambled letters go inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: crashes suggests letters smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a car crash may bring a driver to his senses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashes' scrambles IF ONE into FENOI, which goes 'into' CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong black coffee, served without milk, is the traditional drink for sobering up.

clue.text: A bit of a shock, having bully to heal

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate, bully
animals lick wounds to heal them

explanation.surface: A nasty surprise, being bullied into treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is a shock of hair, not a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft of hair that stands up stubbornly is part of a mop of hair.

clue.text: Make stronger business in leading position

parts.note: a firm is a business
up means ahead, in front

explanation.surface: Strengthening a company by putting it at the top of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To consolidate or strengthen something is a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Racy episode requiring a quick change?

definitions.text: Racy episode requiring a quick change?

parts.words: Racy episode requiring a quick change?
parts.note: racy hints at scandal, but means relating to motor racing, where tyres are swapped fast

explanation.surface: A risqué incident that needs a costume change.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief halt in the pits during a motor race for tyres and fuel.

clue.text: Place to hold course disrupted by hoax

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A racecourse venue upset by a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a course of a meal: the box keeps cooked food hot.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulated box packed with hay that keeps a cooked dish warm.

clue.text: The difference between opposing sides

parts.note: sounds like the gap between two teams, but means the measurement from one edge to the facing edge

explanation.surface: The gap in quality between two rival teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A measurement across something, from one side to its opposite.

clue.text: This should brighten prospects for the motorist

definitions.text: This should brighten prospects for the motorist

parts.words: This should brighten prospects for the motorist
parts.note: prospects reads as hopes, but it means the road ahead that a driver sees at night

explanation.surface: Something that ought to improve a driver's chances.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's front lamp lights up the view of the road ahead.

clue.text: Boiling water, you prepare oatmeal, finishing with this

definitions.text: Boiling water, you prepare oatmeal, finishing with this

indicators.note: finishing picks the final letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A recipe: boil water, prepare oats, and end up with this thin porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin porridge of oatmeal boiled in water.

clue.text: The opposite of the way poetry is written

definitions.meaning: the reverse or converse of something
poems are composed in lines of verse

explanation.surface: Prose is the opposite of how poems are written.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as IN VERSE; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical word for the reverse, and a split phrase saying poems use metre.

clue.text: Forbid one to leave tranquil feast

parts.note: to ban is to forbid

indicators.note: the numeral leaves the calm word, so it is taken out

parts.note: quiet means tranquil
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Banning a single guest from a peaceful dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes I out of QUIET, giving QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: A large formal meal is a feast.

clue.text: Catherine's brief appearance in the pool

definitions.meaning: a short pet form of the name Catherine
the shared fund of stakes in a card game

explanation.surface: Catherine turns up briefly at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' is not water but the pot of money players contribute to; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive of a woman's name, and a communal fund of stakes.

clue.text: Lover of literature, something of a paradox? Yes

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bookish lover asks whether something is a paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a mistress, found mostly in older literature.

clue.text: Hot drink can make one suddenly get excited

definitions.meaning: a warmed mix of beer or spirits with egg and sugar
to lose one's temper or composure, go wild

explanation.surface: A warm drink can make a person suddenly wildly excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make one' is a link joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An old mulled drink of beer and spirits, and slang for losing control.
